analysis.one_liner: Divi's Laboratories makes active pharmaceutical ingredients, custom-synthesis (CDMO) intermediates for global pharma and agrochemical companies, and nutraceuticals, selling mostly to customers outside India.
analysis.whats_happening: The trading window for insiders has been shut since October 1, 2026 ahead of Q2 FY27 (September-quarter) results, due around November 9, 2026 — about three weeks away. At least one brokerage cut its rating from Buy to Hold on October 14, 2026, citing stretched valuation after a strong run. The stock closed at ₹9,144.5 on October 16, 2026, about 5% below its September 23, 2026 peak of ₹9,624 — a pullback, not anything resembling a crash.
analysis.plain_terms: Divi's makes the chemical building blocks that go into other companies' medicines and crop-protection products, and it's increasingly doing specialised custom-made (CDMO) work rather than plain generic chemicals. That shift is lifting both growth and margins. The tension: the market has already priced in a lot of this good news — the stock trades at a much higher earnings multiple than its own 10-year average — so the next few quarters need to keep delivering, not just meet expectations.
analysis.quarters: In the quarter ended June 2026 (Q1 FY27), consolidated revenue rose roughly 28% year-on-year to about ₹3,080-3,144 crore (sources vary slightly) and PAT jumped 65.5% to ₹902 crore, with operating margin expanding to 40.8%. Custom synthesis rose to 60% of revenue from generics' 40%. In the prior reported quarter (Q2 FY26, ended September 2025), revenue was up 17% to ₹2,860 crore while PAT rose a faster 35.1% to ₹689 crore — but that quarter's profit growth was helped by a forex gain of ₹63 crore (versus ₹29 crore a year earlier), so the cleaner EBITDA growth of 25.7% is the better read on core operating performance than the PAT number alone. Management has reaffirmed a double-digit revenue growth target for FY27. Data for the two quarters in between (Q3 and Q4 FY26) could not be verified here.
analysis.performance_read: Returns have been strong in absolute terms — up 39% over 1 year, 154% over 3 years and 76% over 5 years, comfortably ahead of the Nifty in each window. But against its direct peer Laurus Labs, Divi's has badly lagged: Laurus returned 132% (1Y), 407% (3Y) and 218% (5Y) over the same periods. There is no demerger in Divi's history to adjust for — only three stock splits (2007, 2009, 2015), which are already reflected in these return figures. The stock is sitting only 5% below its all-time high, so this is not a drawdown story.
analysis.valuation_read: Divi's is expensive, and expensive for a specific reason: the market is paying up for the custom-synthesis/CDMO growth story and the margin expansion that comes with it. On the 'how expensive' question, sources disagree — GuruFocus puts trailing P/E at about 84x (45% above its own 10-year median of 58x), while another aggregator cites 67.5x; these are not averaged here because the underlying EPS bases likely differ. Either way, the multiple sits well above the stock's own history. Price-to-book of roughly 14.4x reflects a capital-light, high-return business rather than a conventional balance-sheet-heavy one. Whether this is cheap is a separate question from why it is priced this way — the premium only holds up if CDMO growth continues.
analysis.growth_read: Growth here is both volume- and margin-led, and the two are connected: revenue has grown 17-28% year-on-year in the last two reported quarters, while the mix has shifted toward higher-margin custom synthesis (56% to 60% of sales), pushing operating margin up to 40.8% in the latest quarter. This is not a commodity business sitting still on flat volumes with a rising margin — actual sales volumes and the higher-margin product mix are both expanding together, which is the more durable combination.
analysis.health_read: The company is effectively debt-free, with an interest coverage ratio cited near 1,400x given the near-zero debt load. ROE is around 16-17% and ROCE around 21-22%, both above sector medians (roughly 11.7% and 13.5% respectively per one source). Whether profits are converting cleanly into operating cash flow could not be verified here — check the cash flow statement on Screener. Given the lack of debt, the risk to watch is business risk (customer concentration in CDMO contracts, exposure to global pharma/agrochem demand cycles, and forex swings), not financial/balance-sheet risk.
analysis.ownership_read: Promoters (the Divi family) held about 51.8-51.9% as of the latest disclosure, with FIIs around 5.7%, DIIs around 19.2% and public shareholders around 6.5%. The company disclosed on April 6, 2026 that no promoter shares were pledged or encumbered during FY26. No well-known marquee individual investor was found on the register in the sources checked — if one exists, it was not surfaced here.
strengths: PAT grew 35-65% YoY in the last two reported quarters, outpacing revenue growth of 17-28%, reflecting genuine margin expansion, not just one-off items
Company is debt-free with an extremely high interest coverage ratio
Custom synthesis share of revenue rose from 56% to 60% in the latest quarter, reducing reliance on commoditised generic APIs
ROCE of roughly 21-22% sits well above the sector median of around 13.5%
watchpoints: Trailing P/E is elevated at roughly 67-84x against a 10-year median near 58x, leaving little room for disappointment

Stock has massively underperformed peer Laurus Labs over 1, 3 and 5 years (e.g., +39% vs +132% over 1 year), raising the question of whether Divi's deserves its premium relative to faster-growing peers
Dividend yield is just 0.33%, so almost the entire investment case rests on continued earnings growth and multiple re-rating, with no income cushion
A brokerage downgrade from Buy to Hold on October 14, 2026, citing valuation, lands just weeks before Q2 FY27 results
analysis.one_thing: The Q2 FY27 results due around November 9, 2026 — specifically whether custom-synthesis volumes (not just mix shift) keep growing and whether management reiterates its double-digit FY27 revenue guidance, since that is what the current premium valuation is betting on.
analysis.data_notes: Cross-checked Q1 FY27 and Q2 FY26 results across multiple financial news sources; figures were broadly consistent except for minor revenue variance (₹3,080cr vs ₹3,144cr) likely reflecting standalone vs consolidated or total income vs revenue differences. P/E ratio conflicts between sources (83.94x vs 67.51x) and was flagged rather than averaged. Q3 and Q4 FY26 quarterly figures could not be found and are not included. Cash-flow-to-profit conversion was not verified — check Screener directly. Promoter pledge status (nil) is based on an April 2026 company disclosure.
